sights.address: 1384 Ang Mo Kio Avenue 1 / Marymount Road, Singapore 569932
sights.w: One of Singapore's largest urban parks at 62 hectares, and the flagship of PUB's ABC Waters programme — a straight concrete canal was deconcretised into a 3km meandering, naturalised Kallang River with wildflower banks. Biodiversity rose 33% after the 2012 reopening (197 animal species); features include River Plains, Pond Gardens, a water playground, Recycle Hill lookout, dog runs and an allotment garden.

sights.n: Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery
sights.w: Singapore's largest Buddhist monastery, founded 1920 by Venerable Zhuan Dao on Bright Hill (Kong Meng San). Spread over 800,000 sq ft — roughly 14 football fields — its prayer halls, pagodas, Guanyin statue and the ship-like four-storey Venerable Hong Choon Memorial Hall (housing one of Asia's largest bronze Buddha images, 13.8m and 55 tonnes) make it Bishan's great landmark. Also known as Bright Hill Temple.
sights.k: Free entry; vegetarian dining hall on site

sights.address: MacRitchie / Central Catchment Nature Reserve (nearest access via Venus Drive), Singapore
sights.w: The first free-standing suspension bridge of its kind in the region — a 250m span slung 25m high between Bukit Peirce and Bukit Kalang, the two highest points in MacRitchie, for a panoramic view over the rainforest canopy and Upper Peirce Reservoir. A one-way crossing on the wider MacRitchie trail network on Bishan's northern doorstep.

Singapore's oldest reservoir (1868) fringed by a much-loved park on the edge of the Central Catchment — a boardwalk hugging the water, kayaking, the Chemperai and Prunus trails and a 20km network of nature paths leading to the TreeTop Walk. The green lung directly north of Bishan and Sin Ming.

An architectural landmark by LOOK Architects (opened 2006) conceived as a 'tree house' — 16 brightly coloured pods jut from the facade as suspended reading alcoves, with skylights and coloured glass washing the interior in shifting light. Won Singapore's President's Design Award in 2007 and an International Architecture Award in 2009.

sights.n: Kwong Wai Siew Peck San Theng
sights.w: The Cantonese-Hakka cemetery, founded 1870, that gave Bishan its name — 'Peck San Theng' (碧山亭, 'pavilions on the jade hill') became Mandarin 'Bishan'. Once one of Singapore's biggest Chinese cemeteries at 324 acres, it was exhumed from 1982 and rebuilt as a columbarium and preserved ancestral temple; a Heritage Gallery opened in 2018 telling its 150-year story.
sights.k: Temple grounds open daily; heritage gallery free

sights.address: Upper Thomson Road / Old Upper Thomson Road, Singapore 787022
sights.w: A 50-hectare nature park on Bishan's north opened 2019, unique for conserving the ruins of a 1930s-60s Hainan Village — foundations, wells, staircases and old roads along the Ruins and Figs Trail — and as a key refuge for the critically endangered Raffles' banded langur. NParks documented its history with former residents.

A 75-hectare buffer park (opened 2017) off Venus Drive shielding the Central Catchment reserve, with 3.85km of family-friendly boardwalks and trails. The 1.8km Venus Loop threads a crystal-clear forest stream full of freshwater life past a marsh habitat — an easy, accessible gateway to the MacRitchie trails from Sin Ming/Upper Thomson.

A quiet 10-hectare park around Singapore's second-oldest reservoir, wrapped in mature secondary rainforest a short walk from Bishan Park. A 900m boardwalk (built 1998) doubles as an outdoor nature classroom in the Central Catchment forest. (Boardwalk under maintenance to ~Sep 2026; use Casuarina/Jacaranda entrances.)

sights.address: Central Singapore (reserve bounded by Upper Thomson, Sin Ming & Island Club roads), Singapore
sights.w: Singapore's largest nature reserve — some 2,000 hectares of primary and mature secondary rainforest ringing the MacRitchie, Upper/Lower Peirce and Upper Seletar reservoirs. The wild heart of the island on Bishan's northern edge, threaded by the trails, boardwalks and TreeTop Walk that make the town a launchpad for nature outings.

Bishan's civic and retail heart, one of Singapore's early suburban malls (soft-opened Nov 1993). Its name nods to Bishan's old MRT station code N8; it debuted with a Daimaru department store, a Golden Village cineplex and Food Junction's very first outlet, and remains the town centre beside Bishan MRT and the bus interchange.
